newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Champalimaud group launches bid for CPP.
newsitem.headline: Champalimaud group launches bid for CPP.

text.p: Portuguese banks Banco Totta e Acores and Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor jointly with Mundial Confianca, which belong to businessman Antonio Champalimaud, will launch a public offer to buy (OPA) for Totta's subsidiary Credito Predial Portugues, the Champalimaud group said.
The price of the OPA was 1,800 escudos per share, a statement said.
It said CPP would raise its capital by three billion escudos to 33 billion through a subscription of shareholders at a price of 1,800 escudos per share.

"With a capital increase from 30 billion to 33 billion escudos, at 1,800 escudos per share, the Champalimaud group will launch a bid at the same price for all the capital of the institution (CPP)," the statement said.
The refocusing of CPP on the mortgage business is the main objective of the capital increase and bid.

"Until now CPP conducted mortgages and other activities. With a re-focusing exclusively on the mortgage business, we will give an opportunity to shareholders to decide whether they want to continue as shareholders of the bank with this new focus, or not," the statement said.
Champalimaud's Totta has 49.7 percent of the capital of CPP. Totta will guarantee the full amount of the capital increase, the statement said.
In the joint bid, Mundial Confianca will acquire up to 1.8 million of the shares sold and Totta and BPSM will acquire the remainder in equal proportions, a company official said.
Mundial Confianca and BPSM control a 50.15 percent stake in Totta, which will hold more than 50 percent of CPP after the operation.
The company official said the OPA price of 1,800 escudos was the average price of CPP on Lisbon bourse over the past 12 months.
CPP closed today at 2,075 escudos, up 35. Totta closed down nine escudos to 3,468. BPSM closed up 60 escudos to 1,995. Mundial Confianca closed down 12 escudos to 2,978.
